subject: microbiology
title: Echinococcus granulosus: Hydatid Cysts, Casoni Test and Diphyllobothrium

steps.tx: The tiny cyclophyllidean tapeworm **Echinococcus granulosus**, measuring only three to six millimetres with just three proglottids, causes cystic hydatid disease. Dogs and wild canids serve as definitive hosts harboring adult worms, while sheep and herbivores act as intermediate hosts. Humans become accidental dead-end intermediate hosts upon ingesting embryonated tapeworm eggs shed in dog feces.
steps.say: Canids harbor adult tapeworms while accidental ingestion of dog fecal eggs causes hydatid cysts in humans.

vis.caption: Hydatid cyst demonstrating laminated ectocyst, inner germinal layer, and brood capsules [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: Following ingestion, oncospheres penetrate the duodenal mucosa and enter the portal vein to reach the liver, which acts as the primary capillary filter, arresting seventy percent of embryos in the right hepatic lobe. Escaping larvae lodge in the lungs or disseminate systemically. The larva expands slowly over decades into a fluid-filled **hydatid cyst** enveloped by three distinct pathological layers.
steps.say: Oncospheres lodge in the right hepatic lobe, expanding slowly inside a three-layered hydatid cyst.

rows: Vascularized fibrous wall encasing the parasite
Chitinous, non-living elastic white supportive membrane
Metabolically active layer budding brood capsules
Precipitate inside fluid; highly infectious if spilled

steps.tx: The inner cellular germinal layer buds off pedunculated brood capsules into the central cyst cavity. Each capsule generates multiple microscopic invaginated **protoscolices** bearing suckers and a crown of refractile hooklets. Rupture of brood capsules releases these elements into the clear, alkaline, antigenic hydatid fluid, accumulating as a sediment known diagnostically as hydatid sand.
steps.say: The germinal endocyst generates brood capsules filled with protoscolices that precipitate as hydatid sand.

nodes.label: Cellular germinal endocyst buds hollow brood capsules internally
Invaginated protoscolices develop with hooks and suckers inside capsules
Capsule rupture deposits protoscolices and hooklets as hydatid sand

steps.tx: Hydatid cyst fluid contains potent parasitic proteins capable of inducing severe immediate type one hypersensitivity. Spontaneous trauma or accidental needle puncture releasing fluid triggers life-threatening **anaphylactic shock** and widespread secondary peritoneal seeding, where thousands of liberated protoscolices mature into secondary hydatid cysts throughout the abdomen.
steps.say: Fluid leakage triggers catastrophic anaphylactic shock and secondary seeding of multiple peritoneal cysts.

left.title: Immediate fluid rupture risks
points: Severe systemic type I anaphylactic shock

steps.tx: The historical immunological screening tool is the **Casoni test**, an immediate hypersensitivity skin test performed by injecting zero point two millilitres of sterile hydatid fluid intradermally on the forearm. A positive result produces an immediate wheal with pseudopodia within twenty minutes, often followed by a delayed induration at twenty-four hours. Due to low specificity and risk of sensitization, it is now superseded by enzyme immunoassays.
steps.say: The Casoni skin test injected hydatid fluid to produce an immediate wheal, but is replaced by ELISA.

rows: Sterile bovine or sheep hydatid fluid
Historical immediate skin wheal test; high false-positive rate
Purified hydatid antigen B and antigen 5
Modern reference serology; sensitivity over 85% in hepatic cysts
Definitive imaging; detects hydatid sand and floating membranes
Evaluates cyst wall calcification and operative anatomical depth

steps.tx: A minimally invasive alternative to open surgery is the **PAIR technique**, which stands for Percutaneous Aspiration, Injection of scolicidal agent, and Re-aspiration under real-time ultrasound guidance. Following cyst puncture and fluid aspiration, a hypertonic scolicidal solution such as twenty percent sodium chloride or absolute alcohol is instilled for twenty minutes to kill germinal elements before final re-aspiration.
steps.say: The PAIR technique punctures, aspirates, instills scolicidal hypertonic saline, and re-aspirates hepatic cysts.

nodes.label: P: Percutaneous puncture under real-time ultrasound guidance
A: Aspiration of initial clear antigenic hydatid fluid
I: Injection of scolicidal agent (20% hypertonic saline) for 20 minutes
R: Re-aspiration of fluid; patient maintained on oral albendazole

steps.tx: The largest tapeworm infecting humans is the broad fish tapeworm **Diphyllobothrium latum**, which can reach lengths of ten to fifteen metres in the small intestine. Transmission occurs through the consumption of raw, undercooked, or pickled freshwater fish containing plerocercoid larvae (spargana). The ribbon-like strobila contains thousands of broad proglottids wider than they are long.
steps.say: Undercooked freshwater fish transmits the giant Diphyllobothrium tapeworm, which spans over ten metres.

left.title: Diphyllobothrium latum
points: Scolex bears two longitudinal sucking slits (bothria)
Gravid proglottids wider than long with rosette uterus
Operculated eggs with terminal abopercular knob

right.title: Taenia species
points: Scolex bears four cupped muscular suckers
Gravid proglottids longer than wide with branched uterus
Spherical eggs with radial striated embryophore
Requires single intermediate host (pig or cow)

steps.tx: The scolex of Diphyllobothrium latum lacks hooks and suckers, anchoring itself to mucosal folds using two lateral longitudinal sucking grooves called **bothria**. Unlike cyclophyllidean tapeworms whose proglottids detach to release eggs, pseudophyllideans release operculated eggs directly from a central rosette-shaped uterine pore, enabling routine stool microscopy diagnosis.
steps.say: The scolex anchors using two slit-like bothria, discharging operculated eggs from a rosette uterine pore.
